A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fast-SAM3D. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison, including matching relocated ablations.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction-quality and inference-speed measurements on Toys4K, ADT and ISO3D, together with component ablations and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds TRELLIS transfer results, memory measurements, robustness evaluations and five-run uncertainty reporting.

M1.justification: The original Fast-SAM3D procedure in Section 4 is unchanged. Appendix B.1 introduces a specific Fast-TRELLIS adaptation: because TRELLIS lacks explicit layout tokens, its first-stage layout-aware branch is replaced with TaylorSeer-style step caching, while the remaining acceleration designs are transferred.

E1.justification: Toys4K, ADT and ISO3D remain the datasets. v2 adds a degraded-mask input scenario on Toys4K and qualitative multi-view reconstruction examples in Figure 13. Increasing ADT evaluation from 16 to 128 views is a protocol expansion within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the original SAM3D reference and all five acceleration baselines. The new transfer comparison in Table 8 introduces unaccelerated TRELLIS as an evaluated reference, alongside TaylorSeer and Fast3Dcache operating on that backbone.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the evaluation design with a TRELLIS configuration, an additional 128-view ADT test, 50% mask removal with beta values 0.4/0.5/0.6, and overall and stage-wise peak-memory measurements. The original preprocessing, sample counts, metrics and default settings in Appendix A remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices B and F investigate transfer beyond SAM3D, whether caching increases memory demand, stability under broader ADT sampling, and sensitivity to degraded masks and anchoring coefficients. These extend the original component and hyperparameter analyses substantially. The cache-stride, carving-ratio and switching-threshold ablations already existed in v1 and are mainly relocated.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without repeated-run counts or dispersion reporting. Appendix F.3 and Table 14 first state five regeneration/evaluation rounds and report means and standard deviations for SAM3D and Fast-SAM3D across six principal quality metrics. This adds substantial statistical reporting, but does not establish an increase in runs relative to v1.

E6.justification: Table 2 is unchanged. New results include TRELLIS versus Fast-TRELLIS latency of 7.68 versus 3.40 seconds with F1 of 57.19 versus 57.15, and SAM3D versus Fast-SAM3D peak memory of 19.07 versus 17.89 GB. Tables 12–13 add broader-ADT and degraded-mask outcomes, and Figure 13 adds transfer examples. These are additional evaluations, not same-setting gains over v1. Conversely, v2's condensed Table 4 omits CD and ICP-rot entries from v1 Tables 6–7.

T1.justification: The method definitions and derivations in Equations 1–18 and metric formulas in Equations 19–22 are unchanged. No new theorem, formal assumption or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: systematic SAM3D profiling, three complementary training-free acceleration modules, and up to 2.67× speedup with negligible fidelity loss. The additional validation does not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly clarifies that the method accelerates inference rather than improving the underlying reconstruction backbone. Appendix B explains why token and mesh-workload reductions offset cache storage, while Appendix F interprets the new evaluations as evidence of robustness and reproducibility. Existing modality, saliency and spectral interpretations are largely retained.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds limited implementation guidance for transferring the method to TRELLIS and documents overall and per-stage memory requirements. The original A800 hardware specification, hyperparameters, warmup settings and baseline implementation details remain unchanged, as do the code and generated-mesh access statements.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to An et al. on embodied intelligence, Li et al. on interaction techniques in 3D scene generation, and QuantSparse. It also clarifies the method's complementary relationship to reconstruction backbones. Several existing references receive publication metadata updates, which do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: The main narrative and method exposition remain largely intact. Three sensitivity discussions are shortened and moved into Section 5.4, new validation sections reorganize the appendices, and author order, affiliations, publication information and acknowledgements are updated. These are localized structural and editorial revisions.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially expanded and reorganized: v2 adds dedicated transfer, memory, robustness and uncertainty tables plus Figure 13. v1 Tables 6–7 are merged into the compact main-text Table 4 with fewer metric columns, and v1 Table 8 moves into the main text as Table 6. Existing figures are retained, with several resized or repositioned.

improvement.justification: The transfer, memory and robustness evaluations provide useful additional support for applicability and deployment, while five-run uncertainty reporting strengthens confidence beyond v1's point estimates. These extend an already substantial evaluation. The net improvement is limited by brief documentation of the new protocols and the loss of CD and rotation-error entries from the condensed ablation table; the central SAM3D comparison remains unchanged.
